See also: пінгвін

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
пингвин
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English pinguin (obsolete pronunciation), called after the now extinct alcid bird Pinguinus impennis (great auk), which shared physical resemblance with the true penguins from the South hemisphere, first encountered in the 19th century.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [piŋˈɡvin]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -in
  • Syllabification(key): пин‧гвин

Noun

[edit]

пингви́н • (pingvín) m (relational adjective пингви́нов, diminutive пингви́нче)

  1. penguin (flightless seabird of order Sphenisciformes)

[edit]

indefinite пингви́н

count form — пингви́на
pingvína

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • импера́торски пингви́н (imperátorski pingvín, “emperor penguin, genus Aptenodytes”)
  • антаркти́чески пингви́н (antarktíčeski pingvín, “Antarctic penguin, genus Pygoscelis”)
  • ма́лък пингви́н (málǎk pingvín, “little penguin, genus Eudyptula”)
  • очила́т пингви́н (očilát pingvín, “banded penguin, genus Spheniscus”)
  • жълтоо́к пингви́н (žǎltoók pingvín, “yellow-eyed penguin, genus Megadyptes”)
  • качула́т пингви́н (kačulát pingvín, “crested penguin, genus Eudyptes”)

References

[edit]
  • “пингвин”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014
  • “пингвин”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian пингви́н (pingvín), perhaps from Latin pinguis (“fat”).

пингвин • (piñvin)

  1. penguin, Spheniscidae

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian пингвин (pingvin).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pinɡˈʋin/, [pinɡˈʋin]
  • Hyphenation: пинг‧вин

Noun

[edit]

пингвин • (pingvin)

  1. penguin
    • (Can we date this quote?), 7:03 from the start, in Лоло - ичöтик пингвин [Lolo the small penguin], spoken by Мими:
      Но мыйсяма тэ пингвин!
      No myjśama te pingvin!
      What kind of penguin are you!

Etymology

Ultimately from French pingouin, from Dutch pinguïn, from English penguin.

  1. penguin
  2. Pingvin (Soviet anti-zero-G suit)
